You're denying yourself an activity that you've undertaken almost your entire life. This has psychological and chemical ramifications.

There are parts of your brain that are fighting each other right now, and your brain chemistry is FUCKED.

There's a part of your brain called the Amygdala which controls a lot of emotional aspects of yourself. This is also the part of your brain that warns you when you're going to do something bad that has a negative consequence. This is the part of you that has won out and quit drinking because YOU KNOW it is ruining your life due to the numerous experiences you've had in the past.

There are other parts of your brain that do not give a fuck, and want that alcohol again.

They are at odds with each other and while you're drying out from a lifetime of drinking, your brain chemistry is trying to correct itself. This may have something to do with the "alternate reality" you're feeling. Things are trying to even out and it doesn't really feel that great.

I've been in a variation of your position a few times in my life, but not from alcohol. Other things caused this effect in me and it gets better, but a big part of it is finding a purpose or a hobby, like @sanegoatiswear said.

One thing that is really excellent is physical exercise. I've failed on this front myself lately (and I feel it), but I've been in good shape at several times in my life. Arnold Schwarzenegger once said that a great physique is one of the only things in the world you can't lie, steal, cheat or buy to acquire and he's right and it's a great feeling.

I've also got a nephew that came on the scene a couple of years ago and although it is a great deal of responsibility (His dad fucked off so I'm basically his dad), kids make it so you just don't have time for depression and shitty feelings because you've got a responsibility. The real problem is the other adult and dealing with them. The kids are the easier part of that equation.

That obviously doesn't work for everyone, but it did for me.

The short answer is that you've got to find something to fill that gap that not drinking has left. You'll feel better once you can put your time and energy into something you enjoy. It's an almost magical transformation.
